content: It took an 18 wheeler full of incentives to get Denton off his ass. Not to mention, he got little to no sleep last night. "Hm", he Probably related.

Denton lumbered down the long and arduous staircase leading down from his workplace, each irregularity in his gait a protest against the sheer nature of conformity. By the time he got to the bottom, he was jittering with anticipation. This was the 62nd time he walked this path this month. Here, ideas seemed to slowly blossom around him, each one nestled in the man-made forest, waiting to be plucked. His capacity to hold onto ideas was extraordinarily finite, causing him to lose countless to the void. For every 99 abysmal ideas came .5 good ones. Good by his standards, at least.

The Douglas Firs were illuminated by a perfectionist. A perpetual gust of wind kept the lightbulbs swaying and the raindrops weightless. You could catch a stray wire red handed in the bark and still conclude the imperfection was carefully engineered. The occasional passerby halted his conceivably invincible train of thought, rendering an entire world outside his mind. His mind, where he had built a remarkably comfortable place to hang out. It seemed every day there was a new reason to convert a piece of his mind to a playground. If only he was solipsistic enough to live there entirely.
As he drifted downstream along the concrete path, he couldn't shake the feeling that he was living nanoseconds before something monumental.
All you need is a couple.
